The side length of the fabricated cubic cloak device is 100 mm.
The hidden object is a steel ball with a diameter of 38 mm.
The compression ratio of the cloak is 0.172, with the inner hidden region having a diameter of 27.6 mm.
The cloak is fabricated using two types of optical glass: ZLaF78 with a permittivity of 3.61 and ZBaF1 with a permittivity of 2.63.
The regions between the glass segments are filled with water.
The cloak was experimentally demonstrated using a 532 nm laser beam and a transmission pattern as the background.
The recovered image pattern showed that the steel ball hidden inside the cloak was effectively concealed.
The cubic cloak also demonstrated broadband cloaking performance at a wavelength of 650 nm.
The key innovation is the use of a 3D polyhedral transformation and a spatially invariant refractive index discretization approach.
This allows the cloak to be made of isotropic materials rather than the complex anisotropic materials required by previous 3D cloaking designs.
The polyhedral transformation divides the cloak into different segments, each with homogeneous constitutive parameters.
Light bends at the interfaces between these segments, allowing it to be guided around the hidden region.
The spatially invariant refractive index discretization approach replaces the highly anisotropic material parameters with isotropic refractive indices.
This simplifies the fabrication while still allowing the cloak to guide light around the hidden object.
The 3D cloak offers an additional degree of freedom with respect to observation angles compared to 2D cloaks.
